macos.note: The macOS app cannot reach a Yon server with same-origin requests: its pages load from a local origin. Requests to an absolute URL go only to the hosts in tac.outgoing.hosts (NET0, NET1).

windows.note: The Windows app cannot reach a Yon server with same-origin requests: its pages load from a local origin. Requests to an absolute URL go only to the hosts in tac.outgoing.hosts (NET0, NET3).

linux.note: The Linux app cannot reach a Yon server with same-origin requests: its pages load from a local origin. Requests to an absolute URL go only to the hosts in tac.outgoing.hosts (NET0, NET4).

ios.note: The iOS app cannot reach a Yon server with same-origin requests: its pages load from a local origin. Requests to an absolute URL go only to the hosts in tac.outgoing.hosts (NET0, NET1).

android.note: The Android app cannot reach a Yon server: its pages load from a local origin, and only the hosts in tac.outgoing.hosts are reachable (NET0, NET2).

web.note: A browser runs every service in the page, as JavaScript or WebAssembly.

macos.how: Rust and Swift services are linked into the app; other languages run in the page

windows.how: Rust and C# services are linked into the app; other languages run in the page

linux.how: Rust services are linked into the app; other languages run in the page

ios.how: Swift services are linked into the app; other languages run in the page

android.how: Kotlin services are linked into the app; other languages run in the page

macos.note: The macOS build is an unsigned .app bundle. Signing, notarization and a .dmg wait on PKG1.

windows.note: The Windows build is a folder with the .exe. There is no installer or signature yet (PKG4).

linux.note: The Linux build is a folder with the program. There are no packages yet (PKG5).

ios.note: The iOS build runs only in the simulator. Device builds and an .ipa wait on PKG2.

android.note: The Android build is a debug APK. Release APK and AAB builds wait on PKG3.
